findings.headline: Split this one-argument createEffect into compute and apply callbacks (simple shape).
findings.why: Solid 2 requires separate compute and apply callbacks. This callback takes no previous value, registers no cleanup, creates no reactive primitives, and is not async, so the split is usually mechanical.
findings.guidance: Move the reactive reads into the compute callback and return what the side effect needs, then perform the imperative work in the apply callback: createEffect(() => [a(), b()], ([a, b]) => { ... }). Reads left in the apply callback are no longer tracked. createTrackedEffect keeps the one-function shape as an escape hatch, but it may run more than once per change, cannot create primitives, and throws on a pending async read, so prefer the split.

findings.headline: Migrate this two-argument createEffect call.
findings.why: Solid 1 reads the second argument as the initial value, but Solid 2's signature is createEffect(compute, effectFn, options), so the second argument is the apply callback that receives each computed value.
findings.guidance: If the second argument is a Solid 1 initial value, move it to a default parameter of the compute callback and pass the side effect as the second argument: createEffect((prev = INITIAL_VALUE) => compute(prev), (value) => { ... }). If the second argument is already the apply callback, the call is split and needs no change. Stop and ask when you cannot tell which of the two it is.

findings.headline: Restructure this one-argument createEffect before splitting it.
findings.why: Solid 2 requires separate compute and apply callbacks, and this callback reads its previous value, so it cannot be split by moving reads alone.
findings.guidance: Move the previous value to a default parameter of the compute callback, (prev = initial) => ..., or compare in the apply callback, which receives (value, previousValue). Then move the reactive reads into the compute callback and the imperative work into the apply callback.

findings.headline: Restructure this one-argument createEffect before splitting it.
findings.why: Solid 2 requires separate compute and apply callbacks, and this callback registers onCleanup, so it cannot be split by moving reads alone.
findings.guidance: Return the cleanup function from the apply callback instead of calling onCleanup. Then move the reactive reads into the compute callback and the imperative work into the apply callback.

findings.headline: Restructure this one-argument createEffect before splitting it.
findings.why: Solid 2 requires separate compute and apply callbacks, and this callback creates reactive primitives or nested effects, so it cannot be split by moving reads alone.
findings.guidance: Hoist the primitives it creates out of the effect into the owning scope; the apply callback is not an owner for new computations. Then move the reactive reads into the compute callback and the imperative work into the apply callback.

findings.headline: Restructure this one-argument createEffect before splitting it.
findings.why: Solid 2 requires separate compute and apply callbacks, and this callback is async, so it cannot be split by moving reads alone.
findings.guidance: Make the async work the compute callback's result (an async compute is tracked and pending-aware) and keep the apply callback synchronous. Then move the reactive reads into the compute callback and the imperative work into the apply callback.

findings.guidance: Open the referenced callback; the split depends on its body. Then move the reactive reads into the compute callback and the imperative work into the apply callback.
